newsitem.title: HONG KONG: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA WIN, SKIPPER TAYLOR FLOPS AGAIN.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA WIN, SKIPPER TAYLOR FLOPS AGAIN.

text.p: HONG KONG, May 11, Reuter - Embattled Australia captain Mark Taylor failed with the bat again, scoring just four, as his side raced to a four-wicket victory over a Rest of the World X1 on Sunday.

The Australians, on a one-day stopover in Hong Kong on their way to England for the Ashes series, reached their target of 246 with 11.2 overs to spare thanks to a dazzling 116 in 66 balls from opener Mark Waugh.
Waugh completed his century in 91 minutes, hitting 11 fours and nine sixes to all points of the tiny Kowloon Cricket Club ground.
He reached his century with a huge six which carried into the adjoining bowling green where a ladies' match was in progress.
The ferocity of Waugh's hitting carried the Australians to 248 in just 28.4 overs.
A fine 80 by India's Sanjay Manjrekar and an unbeaten 51 by Rohan Gavaskar, son of former Indian opener Sunil Gavaskar, helped the World X1 to 245 for eight.
